newsitem.title: NORWAY: Technical problems depress trade on Oslo Bourse.
newsitem.headline: Technical problems depress trade on Oslo Bourse.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange fell on Tuesday in moderate trade interrupted twice for a total of three hours because of technical problems.
The Oslo bourse Total index, following four consecutive sessions of all-time highs, finished at 1,163.41 points, down 0.2 percent from Monday. Turnover was 870 million crowns.
A bourse spokesman said the disruptions were probably caused by a software problem in the dealing system.
Industrial conglomerate Norsk Hydro, the country's largest listed company, was the most traded share at 105 million crowns. It rose 0.69 percent to 364.50 crowns after slipping over several sessions.
Anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group Kvaerner lost ground after shining for several days on the bourse. Its A share fell 1.2 percent to 425 crowns in trade worth 80 million crowns.
Kvaerner's B share was down one percent at 388 crowns.
Telecommunications group Nera rose six percent to 40.50 crowns following the publication of an analysis by Sundal Collier brokerage which forecast the share would rise 30 percent short-term.
